description:
TYPE: line chart
TITLE: Percentage of U.S. Workers Who Are Union Members, 1983–2017
TEXT IN IMAGE: 
- Title: Percentage of U.S. Workers Who Are Union Members, 1983–2017
- Y-axis: 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%
- X-axis: 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020
DATA: 
- X-axis: Years from 1983 to 2017 (with grid lines marked for 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010, 2020)
- Y-axis: Percentage of U.S. workers, ranging from 10% to 25%
- Line series (Union membership percentage):
  - 1983: ≈20%
  - 1990: ≈16%
  - 2000: ≈13.5%
  - 2010: ≈11.9%
  - 2017: ≈10.7%
KEY FACTS:
- The percentage of U.S. workers who are union members steadily declined from approximately 20% in 1983 to about 10.7% in 2017.
- The highest recorded value on the chart is at the start in 1983 at roughly 20%.
- The lowest recorded value is at the end of the period in 2017 at roughly 10.7%.
- The decline appears relatively consistent across the decades, dropping by roughly half over the 34-year span.
